stem: Phosphoric(V) acid, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$, is used in both inorganic and organic reactions.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ is made in a two-step process from phosphorus.

step 1 Phosphorus reacts with an excess of oxygen to form a white solid.

step 2 The white solid then reacts with water to form $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$.
parts.text: Write an equation for each step.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ is a weak Brønsted-Lowry acid.

Define weak Brønsted-Lowry acid.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ is also formed in the process shown in reaction 1.

reaction 1 $$4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + \text{PH}_3$$

Table 3.1 shows some relevant thermodynamic data.

Table 3.1

| compound | enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}} / \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ | $-972$ |
| $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ | $-1281$ |
| $\text{PH}_3$ | $+9$ |

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Use the data in Table 3.1 to calculate the enthalpy change, $\Delta H_{\text{r}}$, of reaction 1.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Explain why reaction 1 is a disproportionation reaction.

Explain your reasoning with reference to relevant oxidation numbers.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Identify **A**, which reacts with propene in the presence of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ in reaction 2.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction that occurs in reaction 3.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text:

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ also reacts with alcohols to form organophosphates.

Organophosphates are compounds similar to esters. They have the general structure shown in Fig. 3.2.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

Fig. 3.2
parts.text:
Complete the equation to suggest the products of the reaction of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ with methanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$.

$$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 3\text{CH}_3\text{OH} \rightarrow \ldots\ldots\ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Compound **T** is a simple organophosphate.

The mass spectrum of **T** shows a molecular ion peak at $m/e = 182$. This peak has a relative intensity of 12.7.

The relative intensity of the $M+1$ peak is 0.84.

Deduce the number of carbon atoms in **T**.
Hence suggest the molecular formula of **T**.

Assume that phosphorus and oxygen exist as single isotopes.

Show your working.
